newsitem.title: UK: BA cargo says very strong Pacific business.
newsitem.headline: BA cargo says very strong Pacific business.

text.p: Air cargo business in the Pacific area for British Airways Plc's world cargo division is "very strong", managing director Kevin Hatton told Reuters.
He added the seasonal impact of the Chinese New Year holiday in early February had been less than expected and he had had to revise plans to reduce capacity.
The cargo group's overall business is also bouncing back from the third quarter, which saw revenues fall 2.5 percent from October-December 1995 to 145 million stg, he added.

The decline reflected, among other factors, the reorganisation of BA Cargo's airside operations in November-December. "It was a business decision which had a downside but it had to be taken as part of the Change Programme (to improve performance and quality)," Hatton said.
Commenting on the division's key markets, Hatton said Latin America had had "a great year" with both Chile and Colombia standing out.
"I would like extra capacity for Chile but the costs have to be fully justified," he added.

Earlier this week BA Cargo announced a 10 percent increase in ex-UK air cargo rates from March 17 to Latin America and West Africa and a seven percent rise to destinations in Asia, Australia, India and the Middle East.
Rates to the U.S. will go up five percent but they are unchanged to Canada, Europe, South Africa and Kenya. There is also a five percent rise to the rest of Africa.
Turning to the U.S., he said the central region has been a strong market in the past year, while the west coast had been weak.
The European market "is starting to show some encouraging signs" but the continued strength of sterling is expected to hit British exports.
The Middle East and South Asian markets are doing well while Africa is improving, Hatton added.
